transformations.edit: Adapted the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &[T]` parameter and named return for Verus; the executable target body remains the same assert, quotient, split, unsafe chunk conversion, and tuple return flow.
Adapted the Rust `pub const fn` target item to a non-const Verus harness function; no executable control-flow or data-flow step was changed.
Converted Rust `assert!(N != 0, ...)` to Verus `assert(N != 0)` under the same generated precondition; no control-flow path is removed.

Named the Rust split index expression `slice.len() - len * N` as `split_index` after computing `len = slice.len() / N`; this lets proof annotations reuse the exact expression before calling `slice.split_at(split_index)`.

Kept the unsafe chunk-conversion point and modeled only `multiple_of_n.as_chunks_unchecked()` as the target-local boundary `rust_1_96_as_chunks_unchecked_view(multiple_of_n)` after proving `N != 0` and suffix length divisibility.

Inlined the generated shared vocabulary predicates `array_value_view`, `flatten_array_chunks`, and `slice_array_rchunks_partition` so Verus can check the exact prefix-remainder plus flattened chunk suffix postcondition.

Added proof-only arithmetic, sequence-split, and reveal annotations to discharge `split_index < N`, suffix divisibility by N, and prefix/suffix recomposition; these have no executable data-flow or evaluation-order effect.
